subject: Science
chapter: Topic-based: use with whichever Class 9 book your students follow
title: Quick Revision: Tissues

bullets: **Meristematic** (dividing) tissue: apical (tips of root and shoot: length), lateral (cambium: girth), intercalary (base of leaves or internodes).

**Simple permanent:** parenchyma (living, thin walls, stores food; chlorenchyma has chlorophyll; aerenchyma has air spaces for floating), collenchyma (thickened corners, flexibility, e.g. leaf stalk), sclerenchyma (dead, lignin-thickened, hard, e.g. husk of coconut).
**Protective:** epidermis (single layer, waxy cuticle in dry areas, stomata for gas exchange and transpiration); cork (dead cells with suberin, in older stems).

**Complex permanent:** xylem (tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma, xylem fibres) carries water and minerals; phloem (sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres, phloem parenchyma) carries food. Only phloem fibres are dead in phloem.

table: Covers and protects: squamous (skin, lining of mouth), cuboidal (kidney tubules, glands), columnar (intestine), ciliated (respiratory tract)
Blood (plasma + RBC, WBC, platelets), bone, cartilage, ligament (bone to bone), tendon (muscle to bone), areolar, adipose (fat storage)
Striated or voluntary (limbs); smooth or involuntary (stomach, intestine, iris); cardiac (heart; involuntary, contracts and relaxes rhythmically throughout life)
Neurons: cell body, dendrites, axon; carry messages quickly

box: **Remember:** tendon = muscle to bone · ligament = bone to bone · cartilage smooths joint surfaces (also in the nose, ear, trachea)

bullets: Saying xylem carries food. Xylem: water and minerals; phloem: food.

blocks.p: 1. Which tissue makes a plant grow in girth, and where is it found?
2. Name the muscle tissue in the heart, and give one way it differs from muscle in the arm.
